record.title: Harness-Zero reports distilling agent-harness behavior into a model for use under a minimal deployment scaffold
record.summary: Harness-Zero uses an optimized source harness and a harnessing agent to rewrite a student's proposals into trajectories compatible with a fixed, minimal target harness; supervised fine-tuning then aims to retain useful behaviors in the model. Across SpreadsheetBench Verified, AppWorld and USPTO Retrosynthesis, the authors report that Qwen3.5-9B under the minimal harness rises from 23.3% to 44.3% macro-average task success after distillation, above 41.7% for the base model with the optimized harness still attached. The experiments also report an 81.1% versus 78.1% average for agent-as-harness versus code-as-harness in six frontier-model benchmark settings, and 82.3% recovery of 28 mined harness-induced behaviors. These are author-reported results from a single SFT seed; independent reproduction, broader transfer and full cost accounting remain open.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Harness-Zero uses an optimized source harness, a reference harness and a harnessing agent to convert student proposals into supervision compatible with a fixed minimal target harness, then uses supervised fine-tuning to distill resulting behavior into the model.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across SpreadsheetBench Verified, AppWorld and USPTO Retrosynthesis, the authors report Qwen3.5-9B macro-average task success of 23.3% for the base model under a minimal harness, 44.3% after Harness-Zero distillation under that harness, and 41.7% for the base model with the optimized harness attached. They report one SFT seed (42).

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish that harness behaviors can be broadly removed across models and domains, that the distilled approach reduces total compute or cost, or that results are stable across training seeds.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported task-success improvements and behavior-recovery rates have not been independently reproduced.
Reported SFT uses one seed and one Qwen3.5-9B student; uncertainty across seeds, models, domains and target harnesses is unknown.
The paper does not provide a matched accounting of harness evolution, review-agent inference, trajectory generation, fine-tuning and deployment costs.

brief.importance_rationale: If the effect generalizes, transferring useful scaffold behavior into model parameters could change how agents are trained and deployed, reducing dependence on specialized runtime harnesses. Current evidence is a paper-reported result from three domains, one Qwen3.5-9B student and one SFT seed, so broader transfer and cost are unresolved.
limitations: All performance and behavior-recovery results are author-reported; the research desk did not reproduce them.
The distillation experiment trains Qwen3.5-9B separately for three domains with LoRA SFT using seed 42; variance across seeds and student models is not reported in the inspected setup.
The tasks and harnesses are bounded to SpreadsheetBench Verified, AppWorld and USPTO Retrosynthesis with a fixed minimal mini-SWE-agent target harness.
The paper does not establish broad transfer, stable gains under other deployment harnesses, or lower total training and inference cost.

technical.claimed_result: The paper reports macro-average success of 23.3% for the base model under the minimal harness, 44.3% after distillation under that harness and 41.7% for the base model with the optimized source harness still attached. It reports 82.3% average recovery across 28 mined harness-induced behavior patterns.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected manuscript specifies the method, bounded experiments and author-reported results. the research desk did not reproduce them; they remain claimed outcomes.
technical.mechanism: An optimized source harness guides a harnessing agent that rewrites a student's proposed actions into supervision compatible with a fixed target harness. Filtered trajectories are used for supervised fine-tuning; the source harness, reference harness and harnessing agent are removed for the distilled-model deployment evaluation.
technical.regime: Paper-reported tests cover SpreadsheetBench Verified, AppWorld and USPTO Retrosynthesis. Distillation uses Qwen3.5-9B, a minimal mini-SWE-agent harness with one Bash tool, domain-specific LoRA SFT for two epochs and seed 42.
technical.strongest_baseline: Base Qwen3.5-9B under the same minimal target harness at 23.3% macro-average task success; the base model with optimized harness attached reports 41.7%, versus 44.3% after distillation under the minimal harness.

brief.title: Harness-Zero reports distilling agent-harness behavior into a model for use under a minimal deployment scaffold
brief.why_it_matters: Agent capabilities often depend on tools, middleware, memory and workflow scaffolds that are expensive to build and maintain. If useful scaffold behavior can be learned into model weights, deployment might use a simpler fixed harness. This paper reports an initial cross-domain experiment, but does not establish broad transfer, lower total cost or reliable scaffold removal across models.
